details.purpose: Zur Beschreibung der in einer Sequenz beobachteten 'inversion variant' gemäß der HGVS-Nomenklatur.
details.use:
*Use to record the details about an inversion variant of human DNA, observed in a genomic sequence.
This archetype has been specifically designed to be used in the ‘Structured variant' SLOT within the CLUSTER.genetic_variant archetype, but can also be used within other ENTRY or CLUSTER archetypes, where clinically appropriate.
In the examples in this archetype, lower case nucleotides are only intended to highlight the changed positions of the DNA sequence. (en)

Not to be used to record information about variants of non-human DNA, or any kind of RNA or protein.

items.items: Genomic inversion variant
A human genetic sequence change where more than one nucleotide replaces the original sequence with the reverse complement of the original sequence, compared to a genomic reference sequence.
For example: changing 'TCAG' to 'CTGA'.
Start position
Position of the first nucleotide of the inverted range, in relation to the reference sequence.
For example: for a variant where the reference sequence 'CAtcagCCT' is changed to 'CActgaCCT', the start position is 3.
End position
Position of the last nucleotide of the inverted range, in relation to the reference sequence.
For example: for a variant where the reference sequence 'CAtcagCCT' is changed to 'CActgaCCT', the end position is 6.
Inverted sequence
The inverted sequence.
For example: for a variant where the reference sequence 'CAtcagCCT' is changed to 'CActgaCCT', the inverted sequence is 'TCAG'.
Reference sequence
The sequence file used as a reference to describe this variant.
Genetisk variant - Inversjon

En endring i gensekvensen hvor mer enn ett nukleotid (et DNA eller RNA-segment) er tatt ut og satt inn igjen i motsatt orientering (reversering av rekkefølgen i et kromosomsegment), sammenliknet med referansesekvensen.
For eksempel: endring fra 'TCAG' til 'CTGA'.
Startposisjonen
Posisjonen til det første nukleotidet i inversjonen i forhold til referansesekvensen.
*For example: for a variant where the reference sequence 'CAtcagCCT' is changed to 'CActgaCCT', the start position is 3. (en)
Sluttposisjonen
Posisjonen til det siste nukleotidet i inversjonen i forhold til referansesekvensen.
*For example: for a variant where the reference sequence 'CAtcagCCT' is changed to 'CActgaCCT', the end position is 6. (en)
Inverterte sekvensen
Den omvendte/inverterte nukleotidsekvensen på referansesekvensen.
*For example: for a variant where the reference sequence 'CAtcagCCT' is changed to 'CActgaCCT', the inverted sequence is 'TCAG'. (en)
Referansesekvens
Sekvensfilen som har blitt brukt som en referanse for å beskrive varianten.
Genetic inversion variant
A genetic sequence change where, compared to a reference sequence, more than one nucleotide replacing the original sequence are the reverse complement of the original sequence.
*For example: changing 'TCAG' to 'CTGA'. (en)
Start position
*Position of the first nucleotide of the inverted range, in relation to the reference sequence. (en)
*For example: for a variant where the reference sequence 'CAtcagCCT' is changed to 'CActgaCCT', the start position is 3. (en)
End position
*Position of the last nucleotide of the inverted range, in relation to the reference sequence. (en)
*For example: for a variant where the reference sequence 'CAtcagCCT' is changed to 'CActgaCCT', the end position is 6. (en)
Inverted sequence
*The nucleotide sequence of the reference sequence at the given positions. (en)
*For example: for a variant where the reference sequence 'CAtcagCCT' is changed to 'CActgaCCT', the inverted sequence is 'TCAG'. (en)
Reference sequence
The sequence file that has been used as a reference to describe the variant.
